title: Armor Operations
source: lesson-armor.pdf (The Armor School, Fundamentals of Armor Operations); reviewer-armor.pdf

questions.stem: Which of the following defines armor?
questions.key: A combined arms force designed to conduct mounted combat employing armor-protected vehicles as a principal means of accomplishing a ground combat mission
distractors: A force that performs reconnaissance and surveillance and provides security for the unit it is assigned or attached to
A force that closes with the enemy by fire and maneuver to destroy or capture him or repel his assault
A force that neutralizes enemy forces by fire, maneuver and shock effect in coordination with other units
questions.explanation: The lesson defines armor as a combined arms force for mounted combat using armor-protected vehicles as a principal means of accomplishing a ground combat mission.
why: This describes cavalry, one component of armor, not armor as a whole.
This is the mission of mechanized infantry, one component of armor.
This describes the tank, one component of armor.

questions.stem: Which list contains the three sub-components or capabilities of armor in the Philippine Army?
questions.key: Mechanized infantry operations, cavalry operations, tank operations
distractors: Mechanized infantry operations, cavalry operations, artillery operations
Cavalry operations, tank operations, engineer operations
Tank operations, mechanized infantry operations, air defense operations
questions.explanation: The lesson names three sub-components of armor: mechanized infantry, cavalry and tank operations.
why: Artillery is not an armor sub-component; tank operations is the third.
Engineer operations is not an armor sub-component; mechanized infantry is.
Air defense is not an armor sub-component; cavalry is.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of armor?
questions.explanation: The six characteristics are armor protection, firepower, mobility, flexibility, intensive and flexible communication, and shock action. Concealment is not listed.
why: Shock action is one of the six listed characteristics of armor.
Firepower is one of the six listed characteristics of armor.
Flexibility is one of the six listed characteristics of armor.

questions.stem: It is the unit whose mission is to close with the enemy by means of fire and maneuver to destroy or capture him or to repel his assault by fire, close combat, and counterattack.
questions.explanation: This wording is the stated mission of the mechanized infantry unit.
why: Cavalry performs reconnaissance, surveillance and security rather than closing with the enemy.
The tank unit neutralizes the enemy by fire, maneuver and shock effect.
Air cavalry is one of the four basic cavalry designs, whose mission is recon, surveillance and security.

questions.stem: It is the unit whose mission is to close with and neutralize enemy forces by fire, maneuver and shock effect in coordination with other arms.
questions.explanation: Neutralizing the enemy by fire, maneuver and shock effect in coordination with other arms is the mission of the tank unit.
why: Mechanized infantry closes with the enemy to destroy or capture him or repel his assault.
Cavalry's mission is reconnaissance, surveillance and security.
A scout platoon is an organic element of the cavalry troop, not the tank unit.

questions.stem: A division commander wants a force that conserves the combat power of his brigades for engagement where he desires, so that combat power can be concentrated at the decisive place and time. According to the lesson, what role does cavalry play, by its role, in this case?
questions.explanation: Slide 55: cavalry, by its role, is an economy of force with flexible capabilities that let the commander conserve the combat power of divisions or brigades for engagement where he desires.
why: The main effort is where the commander concentrates his combat power; cavalry's role is to help conserve it.
The decisive operation is the action that achieves the mission; the lesson assigns cavalry the economy of force role.
The lesson does not describe cavalry as a reserve; it names economy of force as its role.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines the mission of the cavalry unit?
questions.key: To perform reconnaissance and surveillance and provide security in close operations
distractors: To close with the enemy by fire and maneuver to destroy or capture him or repel his assault
To neutralize enemy forces by fire, maneuver and shock effect in coordination with other arms
To conduct mounted combat using armor-protected vehicles as the principal means of the mission
questions.explanation: The cavalry unit's mission is reconnaissance, surveillance and security in close operations, serving as the commander's eyes and ears.
why: This is the mechanized infantry mission.
This is the tank unit mission.
This is the definition of armor as a whole, not the cavalry mission.

questions.stem: Which list contains the four basic designs into which cavalry is organized?
questions.key: Cavalry squadron/battalion, cavalry troop/company, air cavalry squadron, cavalry troop/company (separate)
distractors: Cavalry squadron/battalion, cavalry troop/company, scout squadron, cavalry troop/company (separate)
Cavalry squadron/battalion, scout platoon, air cavalry squadron, cavalry troop/company (separate)
Cavalry regiment, cavalry troop/company, air cavalry squadron, cavalry troop/company (separate)
questions.explanation: Cavalry is organized into four basic designs: the cavalry squadron/battalion, cavalry troop/company, air cavalry squadron and the separate cavalry troop/company.
why: There is no scout squadron design; the third design is the air cavalry squadron.
A scout platoon is an element within the troop, not one of the four basic designs.
The first design is the cavalry squadron/battalion, not a regiment.

questions.stem: A newly assigned platoon leader of a mechanized infantry platoon loads his platoon headquarters and three squads onto vehicles, with the platoon leader and headquarters in one vehicle. How many AIFVs equip the platoon?
questions.explanation: The mechanized infantry platoon is equipped with four AIFVs: one for the platoon headquarters and one for each of its three mechanized infantry squads.
why: Three vehicles would carry only the squads; the headquarters rides in its own AIFV.
The platoon has one AIFV for the headquarters and one for each of three squads, not five.
Six exceeds the platoon's authorization of one AIFV per element: headquarters plus three squads.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a limitation of mechanized infantry?
questions.key: Infantrymen need sufficient time to mount and dismount
distractors: AIFVs and APCs are better protected than tanks
Dismounted infantrymen are protected from small arms and indirect fire
Armored vehicles can move freely on any avenue of approach regardless of terrain
questions.explanation: Slide 31 lists the limitations: AIFVs and APCs are more vulnerable than tanks, dismounted infantrymen are vulnerable to small arms and indirect fire, infantrymen need time to mount and dismount, and vehicles are restricted to certain avenues of approach.
why: The lesson says AIFVs and APCs are more vulnerable than tanks, not better protected.
The lesson says dismounted infantrymen are vulnerable to small arms and indirect fire.
The lesson says vehicles are restricted to certain avenues of approach because of terrain.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a planning consideration for mechanized infantry?
questions.key: Where to dismount troops (on, before, after)
questions.explanation: The mechanized infantry list includes where to dismount troops, weapon range, objective-to-combat-trains distance, Ex-O or First Sergeant as resource manager, and avenue of approach restrictions.
why: Surface danger zone is a planning consideration for tanks.
Distance from the main body is a planning consideration for cavalry.
SBF positions are a planning consideration for tanks.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a planning consideration for tanks?
questions.explanation: Tank planning considerations are surface danger zone, direct fire control measures, SBF positions, cover against enemy air, and employment against tanks or armored vehicles. Distance from main body belongs to cavalry.
why: Surface danger zone is the first tank planning consideration.
Direct fire control measures is a listed tank planning consideration.
Cover against enemy air is a listed tank planning consideration.

questions.stem: A mechanized battalion receives a 6x6 wheeled APC acquired in 2024 under the Horizon 2 Project, armed with a 12.7 mm HMG and a 7.62 mm co-axial GPMG. Which vehicle is this?
questions.explanation: The lesson's equipment slide lists the Guarani 6x6 wheeled APC, acquired 2024 under the Horizon 2 Project with a 12.7 mm HMG and 7.62 mm GPMG.
why: Sabrah is the light tank on the ASCOD II platform, not a wheeled APC.
The Commando V-150S is a separate armored vehicle, not the wheeled APC under Horizon 2.
The Simba fighting vehicle is listed separately from the Guarani 6x6 wheeled APC.
